bridgeDecisions.Q3: OWNER CHANGED THIS ONE: where the engine and the tablet differ because of a business rule, the ETP Reporting Engine's figure counts. (given in chat, 2026-11-12)
bridgeDecisions.Q4: Keep the four-report XLSX import as fallback for two monthly closes after go-live; one source per store and period. (given in chat, 2026-11-12)
bridgeDecisions.Q5: HEMW stays blocked on both paths until the engine holds HEMW data the owner has checked. (given in chat, 2026-11-12)
bridgeDecisions.Q6: Version 1: exactly the four reports (R003, R013, R022, R025) with today's columns, plus engine totals. (given in chat, 2026-11-12)
bridgeDecisions.Q7: Export by Owner only; import by Owner, or Store Manager with Owner reauthentication. (given in chat, 2026-11-12)

bridgeDecisions.Q9: Carrier: USB cable, OTG stick or synced cloud folder. The app never goes online. (given in chat, 2026-11-12)
bridgeDecisions.Q10: Remove INTERNET permission if nothing needs it (Wave 5 is checking). (given in chat, 2026-11-12)
bridgeDecisions.Q11: Later: dummy-data build to use a synthetic test-key-signed pack through the real gateway. (given in chat, 2026-11-12)

filesNotVisibleToAnalyser.knownIssueOnceTracked: Audit check A2-04 (the same named domain constant and value defined in two product files) would have failed once the four Wave 6 bridge files were tracked, because VERSION = 1 was defined in etp-bridge-compare, etp-bridge-facade, etp-bridge-pack-verifier, etp-bridge-trust and the existing etp-native-store, and STORE = WLMHW in etp-bridge-compare and etp-bridge-facade. Fixed in step F1 (2026-11-12) by a purely internal rename of the file-local constants (TRUST_VERSION, PACK_VERSION, COMPARE_VERSION, FACADE_VERSION, COMPARE_STORE, FACADE_STORE); no exported name, public VERSION property, refusal code, message or behaviour changed, and the ledger figures in this record are identical with and without the rename (the bridge files are invisible to the analyser until tracked, and the rename adds or removes no failure-posture token). The bytes and sha256 of the four files in filesNotVisibleToAnalyser are the post-rename values.

trustAndGateStatement.state: declared in code with an empty trust anchor; closed
trustAndGateStatement.shippedTree: www/etp-bridge-trust.js holds a frozen empty key list. gate() returns CLOSED with ETP_BRIDGE_TRUST_ANCHOR_ABSENT, and every pack is refused with ETP_BRIDGE_TRUST_GATE_CLOSED before any file read or PIN prompt.
trustAndGateStatement.evidenceCheckG: Check G, run in W4 on 2026-11-12: the trust file evaluated in a vm context shows isFrozen true, key list frozen and empty, gate CLOSED / ETP_BRIDGE_TRUST_ANCHOR_ABSENT, no test-seam export, global non-writable and non-configurable; no PEM public key, no JWK token and no 65-byte 0x04 point (base64 or hex) in www/, build-overrides/ or android/app/src/main.
trustAndGateStatement.registration: The gate is NOT registered in scripts/audit/config.mjs (that edit would fail audit comparison C-09 EXTERNAL_GATE_SET_CHANGED and change the audit-tooling fingerprint). scripts/audit/config.mjs is byte-identical to its pre-wave state (sha256 18270ccb605f1a406f135543ecb8ab56bf0f88c050ea47fde0af8d77f217c82d). Registering it is an owner step after the commit together with a re-freeze of the audit tooling.
trustAndGateStatement.realKey: The owner creates the real bridge signing key himself later (Q1). Nothing in this wave creates, stores or embeds it.
trustAndGateStatement.keyHygieneScan: Check K, run in W4 on 2026-11-12 over the repository tree (excluding node_modules, .git, android build output, graphify-out and any .audit-secrets folder), over the W4 patch and over the W4 untracked snapshot: 0 private key blocks, 0 private JWKs, 0 files named *.pem *.p8 *.pfx *.jks *.keystore *.key. Non-key matches, all explained: tests that build detection patterns or synthetic strings, the pre-existing tracked public audit-signer key in scripts/audit/trusted-evidence-signers.mjs, and an ignored Node compile cache under .tmp-audit-tests that holds a placeholder block. The orchestrator repeats the scan on the staged diff before each commit and before the push.
trustAndGateStatement.doesNotClose: WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 verification on the Samsung Tab S7 WebView is not verified. Native acceptance of a bridge-built manifest is not verified.

testKeyStatement: The throwaway test key pair is generated in memory at run time by the tests and the synthetic-pack generator, as a non-extractable WebCrypto key; only the raw public point is exported; no private key is written to the repository or to any file this wave delivers (owner decision B-4; the CLAUDE.md rule against creating keys concerns the APK signing key). The test public key reaches the verifier only through a test-only seam (the CommonJS create() of the verifier) that the built app cannot reach.

behaviourStatement.published: Nothing from a pack is published to operational consumers. The engine is not an approved source (Q2): that needs compare mode to match the XLSX imports for one full month of WLMHW and a new authority record, which is not given.
behaviourStatement.calculations: No calculation anywhere changes (Q3). Row totals must match exactly or the pack is refused. Incentives and payroll are untouched.
behaviourStatement.stores: HEMW is blocked on both paths (Q5). The service store AW330 and every other store code are refused. One source per store and period (Q4); the XLSX import is unchanged.
behaviourStatement.roles: Import by Owner, or Store Manager with Owner reauthentication through the existing reauthentication (Q7). Export is engine-side and not in this wave (Q12).
behaviourStatement.carrier: The pack is read from a file the user picks (USB, OTG or a synced folder). The app never goes online (Q9); no network access is added.
